newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid in talks to buy Kwong Yik stake.
newsitem.headline: Rashid in talks to buy Kwong Yik stake.

text.p: Malaysian stockbroking group Rashid Hussain Bhd said on Friday that it has entered into negotiations with Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) for the acquisition of its entire equity interest in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd.
No price was mentioned, and Rashid requested in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange that the trading in its shares continue to be suspended.
Maybank, Malaysia's largest banking group, owns a 75 percent equity stake in smallish bank Kwong Yik.
Shares of Rashid, Maybank, Kwong Yik and DCB Holdings Bhd were suspended from Monday. Rashid owns 20.4 percent of DCB, also a banking group.
Analysts said the announcement was positive for Rashid but not unexpected as the market has speculated on the deal all week.
"The acquisition confirms the trend in the industry, particularly amongst the smaller banks. It's a step (forward) in the whole direction," said John Engle, HG Asia managing director.
Analysts speculated that Maybank was expected to ask anything from 6.50 to 12.00 ringgit for each Kwong Yik share, valuing the deal at 2.13 billion to 3.93 billion ringgit.
Kwong Yik stock was last traded at 6.95 ringgit.

Analysts had said that Maybank was expected to sell its stake in Kwong Yik to Rashid to raise funds, as well as to meet a Malaysian banking requirement which disallows a bank from holding two banking licences.
If the deal were to go through Rashid is expected to inject Kwong Yik into DCB, the parent of DCB Bank Bhd.
"This is the first stage of a more complex deal involving DCB Bank and perhaps Bank Bumiputra," said Stephen Weller, director of strategy at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
There has also been speculation that the country's second largest bank, Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd, may be injected into DCB as part of a larger restructuring of the Malaysian banking industry.
If the deal goes through, the resultant merged bank would be Malaysia's third largest as measured by assets, analysts said.
